mei: Quick sanity check — hitting partial JSON/parsing failures in the Python SDK when the auth token refresh happens mid-stream. Happens on long chat streams.
mei: minimal symptom: after ~10s of tokens we get `JSONDecodeError` while assembling events.
praveen: ugh same class of issue. Are you using requests `iter_lines()` or `response.raw`?
mei: iter_lines right now. code is basically:
```python
for chunk in resp.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
    if not chunk:
        continue
    # chunk contains partial `data: ...` lines sometimes
    buf += chunk
    try:
        obj = json.loads(buf)
        handle(obj)
        buf = ""
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        # waiting for more
        pass
```
alex: This pattern is ok but breaks if the stream inserts keepalive/comments or an auth retry that returns a short 204 then reconnect. You might be accidentally concatenating frames across logical boundaries.
praveen: two practical fixes we use: 1) parse by SSE framing (split on double-newline between events and parse only `data:` lines), 2) keep an incremental buffer per event and only json.loads the full `data` payload.
praveen: i.e. extract `data:` prefix then accumulate until the event boundary. Example parse snippet:
```python
# pseudocode
for raw in resp.iter_lines():
    line = raw.strip()
    if line.startswith('data:'):
        event_buf += line[len('data:'):]
    elif line == '':
        # event boundary
        try:
            j = json.loads(event_buf)
            handle(j)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            # still partial, keep buffering
            pass
        event_buf = ''
```
mei: hmm we're doing that but the token refresh path inserts a 204 (no content) and the client auto-reconnects; when reconnect happens some leading bytes from new session are read into old buffer in our current code.
alex: that's a race in the streaming reconnect logic. You need to reset parser state on reconnect or treat HTTP status changes as event boundaries.
sam: also watch for chunked transfer encoding split across UTF-8 multibyte chars — but that's less common in JSON token failures, more like mojibake errors.
praveen: for backpressure: are you processing on the socket reader thread? If handling is slow it builds up. We solved by putting parsed events into an asyncio.Queue(maxsize=500) and awaiting queue.put — that naturally exerts backpressure on reader.
mei: implementing queue helped latency spikes, thx. Any suggestions for auth refresh during stream?
alex: simplest: use an auth refresh callback that triggers a graceful reconnect: send a special `:reconnect` comment or close the connection server-side with a dedicated code to signal client to resume with new token. If you control server, send `event: auth_refresh\n` then close.
praveen: if you can't change server, client should detect 401/403 or 204 and immediately reset parser state and open new connection. Also ensure any leftover partial bytes are discarded.
mei: PR incoming — added explicit state.reset() on non-200 responses and an exponential reconnect with jitter. pinging @alex for quick review on the reconnect/state reset bits.
alex: will review in ~30m. quick manual test: run long stream, force token rotate via curl and confirm no JSONDecodeError.
ci-bot: Build passed for branch `mei/stream-auth-fix` (tests: streaming-parser). :white_check_mark:
mei: thanks! i'll run the manual curl test and post logs if it still fails.
praveen: one more tip: when trying to detect incomplete JSON, using a char-balance heuristic (count `{` vs `}`) can reduce false-positive loads for tiny traffic bursts, but it's brittle. Prefer event framing.
sam: and don't forget to handle `:\n` comment keepalives — treat them as no-op event boundaries so parser doesn't hang.
mei: perfect. I'll push the manual test results here. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
mei: (follow-up) manual test succeeded after state reset on 204, no JSONDecodeError on token rotation. leaving PR up for review.
